Everything in this course applies to the work you are already doing. Every piece of academic work you start needs ideas found and shaped, more than one approach weighed, and sources read for what they could mean; the students who use creative methods on purpose are the ones whose work grows richer from one task to the next. Treat what follows as being about your own essays, reports and reading, not about study in the abstract.

The same habits carry into professional practice. Wherever you are asked to solve a problem, plan a piece of work, or make sense of evidence, generating options, staying flexible and seeing fresh connections are valued. The creative methods you are about to practise are ones you keep using long after you graduate.
